reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an educational discussion of how YouTube ad revenue is calculated, with the speaker explicitly qualifying the estimated per-view amount as variable and not applicable to every channel. The speaker promotes a website and YouTube-success material and mentions the possibility of a six-figure channel, but the available video evidence describes no required payment, typical-results claim, eligibility condition, guaranteed outcome, or deceptive transaction. Requests to subscribe, comment, or visit related content are presented as ordinary audience engagement and learning prompts.

citations.quote: In this video we'll be talking about how much a single view is worth to a creator on youtube.
Just how much money a single view generates a YouTuber when someone watches an ad on their video.
this number I'm about to give you isn't 100% accurate for every single channel on youtube
if you really want to learn more about YouTube and maybe even start your own successful YouTube channel that actually makes you six figures a year, then check out my website, shawnmalkoo.com
EXCLUSIVE YouTube Success Guide: https://youtube.shawnmalkou.com/

opening.argument: The video does more than explain advertising math: it pairs an income-oriented promise with a direct route to the speaker's website. Viewers are told they might start a successful YouTube channel that “actually makes you six figures a year,” and are immediately instructed to “check out my website.” The description separately advertises an “EXCLUSIVE YouTube Success Guide” with an external link. That creates a clear solicitation structure: pursue a potentially substantial creator income opportunity by following the promoted web destination. The discussion of a per-view figure gives the pitch an analytical appearance, but it does not establish that the promoted path can deliver the highlighted outcome or explain the conditions required to obtain it.

citations.quote: maybe even start your own successful YouTube channel that actually makes you six figures a year, then check out my website
EXCLUSIVE YouTube Success Guide: https://youtube.shawnmalkou.com/
I'm about to probably absolutely wow you guys right now because most people don't know what this is

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the presentation educational does not remove the commercial linkage. The same presentation that supplies the revenue figure directs viewers to the speaker's website and success material, while the six-figure possibility is used to motivate that visit. The absence of an explicit payment demand in the excerpt does not prove the promoted offer is harmless; it leaves the material and conditions of the external offer unexamined.

citations.quote: then check out my website, shawnmalkoo.com
EXCLUSIVE YouTube Success Guide: https://youtube.shawnmalkou.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted six-figure language is conditional and framed as something a viewer might learn to pursue, not a guaranteed payment for clicking. The video also expressly limits its calculation to ad revenue and warns that the number is not universal. Nothing cited establishes that visiting the website requires payment, registration, deposit, or any guaranteed result.

citations.quote: this number I'm about to give you isn't 100% accurate for every single channel on youtube
maybe even start your own successful YouTube channel that actually makes you six figures a year

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an external website, an “EXCLUSIVE” success guide, and a prominent six-figure earning possibility. The speaker first presents a dramatic money-centered hook, saying the number will “absolutely wow” viewers, then channels interest toward his own website and course. The underlying calculation is based on three channels, yet viewers are invited to connect it with building a successful channel capable of six-figure income. That combination can make promotional material look like neutral research while using an attractive earnings outcome to drive traffic. The low per-view figure does not cure the concern, because the broader appeal is the possibility of scaling a channel into substantial income through the promoted guidance.

citations.quote: I'm about to probably absolutely wow you guys right now because most people don't know what this is
maybe even start your own successful YouTube channel that actually makes you six figures a year
EXCLUSIVE YouTube Success Guide: https://youtube.shawnmalkou.com/
I had a case study where I took monthly ad revenue, from 3 different youtube channels

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. The relevant pattern is the combination of sensational money framing, a success-income reference, and an external guide promoted by the same speaker. A disclaimer about variability may qualify the arithmetic, but it does not qualify the promotional implication that the linked material can help viewers reach the highlighted level of earnings.

citations.quote: lots of factors can change this number
check out my website, shawnmalkoo.com

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The alleged risk pattern still lacks a concrete scam mechanism. The speaker discloses that the estimate comes from only three channels and repeatedly says factors can change it; he also states that not all views are monetized. Those qualifications undermine a deceptive universal-income claim, and the supplied material does not show that the guide guarantees six figures or demands money for access.

citations.quote: this number I'm about to give you isn't 100% accurate for every single channel on youtube
not all views are monetized

opening.argument: Although the video adopts the role of an explainer, its structure functions as promotion for the speaker's YouTube-success products and website. It invites viewers to subscribe, points them to an earlier riches video, advertises an online course for more detail, and connects visiting the website with the prospect of creating a channel that “actually makes you six figures a year.” The revenue lesson therefore serves as a credibility-building entry point into a commercial funnel: establish authority with a specific earnings calculation, emphasize that viewers may be missing valuable information, and direct interested viewers to the speaker's own materials. The educational framing does not by itself establish that the promoted opportunity is substantiated.

citations.quote: if you are new around here consider smashing that subscribe button
I've broken this discussion down in so much more detail in my online course to Youtube Success
then check out my website, shawnmalkoo.com
actually makes you six figures a year

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes ordinary engagement prompts but overlooks the more targeted promotion: the speaker says further detail is in his online course, then directs viewers to his website beside a six-figure channel outcome. That is materially different from merely asking for a subscription or comment. The apparent lesson can reasonably be read as lead-generation for a paid or otherwise commercial success offering whose actual terms are not shown.

citations.quote: I've broken this discussion down in so much more detail in my online course to Youtube Success
then check out my website, shawnmalkoo.com

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and scam are not interchangeable. The video openly identifies the scope as ad revenue, explains that the estimate is based on three channels, and says the figure is not accurate for every channel. The six-figure statement is a possibility attached to learning more, not evidence of a guaranteed return, required purchase, or deceptive transaction.
